zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Ṣād
Meccan
﷽
﴿ص﴾: it has been read with fatḥa, with kasra, and with the dāl made quiescent (sukūn), and this last is the most common reading. Whoever makes it quiescent reads "صادْ" as one of the letters of the alphabet (ḥurūf al-hijāʾ), the dāl being treated as in a pause (waqf); we have explained this under His saying "الـم", I mean the chapter on the letters of the alphabet. Its meaning is "Allah is the Truthful (اَلصّادِقُ اللَّهُ)". It has also been said that it is an oath.
And His saying: ﴿والقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; the meaning is: "I swear by Ṣād, and by the Qur'an possessed of remembrance (أُقْسِمُ بِصادِ، وبِالقُرْآنِ ذِي الذَّكَرِ)". Whoever gives it fatḥa does so in two ways: it may be a fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters (iltiqāʾ al-sākinayn), and it may be in the sense of "recite Ṣād (اُتْلُ صادَ)", with "صادَ" being a name of the sūra, a diptote. Whoever gives it kasra does so in two ways: because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, or with kasra in the sense of "confront (ṣādi) the Qur'an with your deeds (صادِ القُرْآنَ بِعَمَلِكَ)", from your saying "صادى، يُصادِي" when one faces and matches [something]; one says "صادَيْتُهُ" when you have faced him.
The answer (jawāb) to His saying ﴿ص والقُرْآنِ﴾ is ﴿إنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخاصُمُ أهْلِ النّارِ﴾ [Ṣād: 64]. Some people said: the answer is ﴿كَمْ أهْلَكْنا مِن قَبْلِهِمْ مِن قَرْنٍ﴾ [Ṣād: 3], its meaning being "لَكَمْ أهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهم مِن قَرْنٍ" (how many a generation We indeed destroyed before them); since the speech between the two became long, the lām was omitted.
The meaning of "والقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ" is: "possessed of mention and honour (ذِي الذِّكْرِ والشَّرَفِ)". It has also been said that "ذِي الذِّكْرِ" means: in it are mentioned the stories of the former and the later peoples, and what is needed concerning the lawful and the unlawful.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿أمْ لَهم مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, that is: nothing of that is theirs. ﴿فَلْيَرْتَقُوا في الأسْبابِ﴾, that is: if they claim anything of that, then let them ascend by the means (asbāb) that would bring them to the heaven. It is also possible that it means "let them ascend by these means that have been mentioned, which none but Allah possesses".

zajjaj:11-11.t: Then Allah promised His Prophet, upon him be peace, victory over them, and said: ﴿جُنْدٌ ما هُنالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِنَ الأحْزابِ﴾. "ما" is redundant (laghw); the meaning is: "جُنْدٌ هُنالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِنَ الأحْزابِ" (a host there, routed, of the confederates).

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿وَفِرْعَوْنُ ذُو الأوْتادِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that Pharaoh had ropes and stakes on which people would perform for him «[Translator's note: «يُلْعَبُ لَهُ عَلَيْها», literally "played on for him".]».

zajjaj:3-3.t:
﴿فَنادَوْا ولاتَ حِينَ مَناصٍ﴾: it has come in the exegesis (tafsīr): "and it was no time for calling out (وَلاتَ حِينَ نِداءٍ)". The people of the language said: "and it was no time for escape (وَلاتَ حِينَ مَنجًى)" and "no escaping (لا فَوْتَ)". One says "ناصَهُ، يَنُوصُهُ" when something has escaped him. In the exegesis, "لاتَ حِينَ نِداءٍ" means: "it was no time for a calling out that would save". It is also permissible to read "لاتَ حِينُ مَناصٍ" [with nominative], and the nominative is good.
The pause (waqf) on it is "لاتْ", with tāʾ; al-Kisāʾī pauses on it with hāʾ, "لاهْ", because he makes it the hāʾ of the feminine. The correct pause on it is with tāʾ, and this tāʾ is analogous to the tāʾ in the verb when you say "ذَهَبْتُ، وجَلَسْتُ", and in your saying "رَأيْتُ زَيْدًا ثُمَّتَ عَمْرًا" (I saw Zayd, then ʿAmr). So the tāʾ of particles is equivalent to the tāʾ of verbs, because in both places the tāʾ has entered upon something that is not declined (lā yuʿrab) and is not on the path of nouns.
If someone says: we treat it like their saying "كانَ مِنَ الأمْرِ ذَيْهْ" and "ذَيْهْ" (such-and-such happened), for this is a hāʾ in pause, and this is a hāʾ that has entered upon a noun which is not declined. «[Translator's note: the source gives no explicit reply to this objection.]»
They have also permitted the genitive (khafḍ), saying "لاتَ أوانٍ", and they recited, by Abū Zubayd:
؎طَلَبُوا صُلْحَنا ولاتَ أوانٍ ∗∗∗ فَأجَبْنا أنْ لَيْسَ حِينَ بَقاءِ
(They sought peace with us when it was no longer the time, so we answered that it was no time for survival.)
What Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] recited to us — and so he narrated it — was:
طَلَبُوا صُلْحَنا ولاتَ أوانٌ
and he mentioned that the kasra has also been narrated.
As for the accusative, it is on the basis that it [لات] operates as "لَيْسَ" operates; the meaning is "and the time is not a time of escape (وَلَيْسَ الوَقْتُ حِينَ مَناصٍ)". Whoever puts it in the nominative with it makes "حِينَ" the subject (ism) of "لَيْسَ" and implies the predicate (khabar), in the sense of "there is no time of escape for us (لَيْسَ حِينُ مَنجًى لَنا)". Whoever puts it in the genitive makes it indeclinable (mabnī) with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, just as they said "قَدِ لَكَ" and made it indeclinable on kasra.
The meaning is "it is not the time of our escape and the time of our deliverance (لَيْسَ حِينُ مَناصِنا وحِينُ مَنجانا)". So when he said "وَلاتَ أوانَ", he made it in the sense of "it is not the time of our [proper] time (لَيْسَ حِينَ أوانِنا)"; when the muḍāf ilayhi «[Translator's note: the source says «المضاف» (the muḍāf), though what is dropped from «أوانِنا» is the attached pronoun, i.e. the muḍāf ilayhi.]» was omitted, it was made indeclinable on the pause form, then given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The kasra is anomalous (shādhdh), resembling an error in the view of the Basrans; Sībawayh and al-Khalīl did not narrate the kasra, and what is followed in practice is the accusative and the nominative.
Al-Akhfash said that in "لاتَ حِينَ مَناصٍ" its accusative is by "لا", just as you say "لا رَجُلَ في الدّارِ" (there is no man in the house), and the tāʾ entered for the feminine.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقالَ الكافِرُونَ هَذا ساحِرٌ كَذّابٌ﴾, up to His saying: ﴿لَشَيْءٌ عُجابٌ﴾ [Ṣād: 5], in the sense of "wondrous (عَجِيبٌ)". "عُجّابٌ" is also permissible, in the sense of "عَجِيبٌ"; one says "رَجُلٌ كَرِيمٌ، وكُرّامٌ، وكُرامٌ" (a generous man).
This is a report of what a group of the notables of Quraysh said: «When Abū Ṭālib fell ill with the illness in which he died, Abū Jahl ibn Hishām and a group of Quraysh came to visit him, and they complained to him about the Prophet ﷺ and said: He insults our gods and does such-and-such. So Abū Ṭālib reproached him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "I am calling you to a word by which the Arabs will submit to you, and by which the non-Arabs will pay you the jizya." Abū Jahl said: Yes, and ten [more], by way of mockery, meaning: we will say it and ten others with it. So he said: "There is no god but Allah (لا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ)." They said: Has he made the gods one God? Then they rose and left their gathering, saying to one another: Walk on and be steadfast for your gods.»

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying: ﴿وانْطَلَقَ المَلأُ مِنهم أنِ امْشُوا﴾: its meaning is: that is, "walk on (اِمْشُوا)"; its interpretation is: they say "walk on". It is also permissible [to understand it as] "وانْطَلَقَ المَلَأُ مِنهم بِأنِ امْشُوا" (the notables among them went forth with "walk on"), that is, with this saying.

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿ما سَمِعْنا بِهَذا في المِلَّةِ الآخِرَةِ﴾ is also a report of what they said, that is: we have not heard of this in Christianity, nor in Judaism, nor in what we found our forefathers upon. ﴿إنْ هَذا إلا اخْتِلاقٌ﴾, that is: nothing but a fabricated saying (taqawwul).

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿أأُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ مِن بَيْنِنا﴾, that is: how has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us? That is: how has the Qur'an been sent down to Muhammad from among us?! ﴿بَلْ هم في شَكٍّ مِن ذِكْرِي﴾, that is: they say what they hold only while being in doubt.

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His saying: ﴿أمْ عِنْدَهم خَزائِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ﴾: if someone asks: what is the connection of ﴿أمْ عِنْدَهم خَزائِنُ﴾ with His saying ﴿بَلْ هم في شَكٍّ مِن ذِكْرِي﴾ [Ṣād: 8], or with His saying ﴿أأُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ مِن بَيْنِنا﴾ [Ṣād: 8]? [The answer is that] this is evidence of their envy of the Prophet ﷺ for the favour of prophethood that Allah gave him. So Allah made known that sovereignty belongs to Him and the message is His to give; He chooses whom He wills, gives sovereignty to whom He wills, and sends down rain and mercy upon whom He wills. So He said: ﴿أمْ عِنْدَهم خَزائِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ﴾, that is: they do not have that.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿ما لَها مِن فَواقٍ﴾, and "فُواقٍ", with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the fāʾ, that is: "it has no return (ما لَها مِن رُجُوعٍ)". "اَلْفُواقُ" is the interval between two milkings of the she-camel, and it too is derived from [the sense of] returning, because the milk returns to the udder between the two milkings. "أفاقَ مِن مَرَضِهِ" (he recovered from his illness) is from this, that is, he returned to health; so "الفَواقُ" is from this as well.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
﴿وَقالُوا رَبَّنا عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا﴾: "اَلْقِطُّ" is the share (naṣīb). Its origin is the written sheet (ṣaḥīfa) in which something due to reach a person is written for him. Al-Aʿshā said:
؎وَلا المَلِكُ النُّعْمانُ يَوْمَ لَقِيتُهُ ∗∗∗ بِغِبْطَتِهِ يُعْطِي القُطُوطَ ويَأْفِقُ
(Nor King al-Nuʿmān, on the day I met him in his prosperity, giving out written grants and bestowing generously.)
"يَأْفِقُ" means: he gives in excess (yufḍil). This is the explanation of their saying "عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا", and it is like their saying: ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ مِن عِنْدِكَ فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32], to the end of the verse. It has also been said that when they heard that the believer will be given his book in his right hand and the disbeliever will be given his book in his left hand, so that the believer is made happy and the disbeliever is ruined, they said: "Our Lord, hasten for us our share (عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا)".
The derivation of "اَلْقِطُّ" is from "قَطَطْتُ", that is, "I cut (قَطَعْتُ)"; and likewise the share is simply a piece (qiṭʿa) of a thing.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
﴿واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ ذا الأيْدِ﴾: "possessed of strength (ذا القُوَّةِ)". His strength in worship was the most complete strength: he used to fast one day and break his fast one day, and that is the most severe fasting, and he used to pray half the night.
﴿إنَّهُ أوّابٌ﴾: "one who returns to Allah often (رَجّاعٌ إلى اللَّهِ كَثِيرًا)". "اَلْآيِبُ" is the one who returns, and "اَلْأوّابُ" is the one who returns often.

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿إنّا سَخَّرْنا الجِبالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ بِالعَشِيِّ والإشْراقِ﴾: "اَلْإشْراقُ" is the rising of the sun and its shining. One says "شَرِقَتِ الشَّمْسُ" when the sun rises, and "أشْرَقَتْ" when it shines. It has also been said that "شَرِقَتْ" and "أشْرَقَتْ", when it rises, have one meaning; but the first is more common.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿والطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً كُلٌّ لَهُ أوّابٌ﴾: the mountains used to repeat the glorification (tasbīḥ) back, and so did the birds. It is possible that the hāʾ [in لَهُ] refers to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, that is: "all glorify Allah — the birds, the mountains and David glorify Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and repeat the glorification". And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that "كُلٌّ لَّهُ أوّابٌ" means: all of them repeat the glorification with David, answering him; whenever he glorified, the mountains and the birds glorified with him.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
﴿وَشَدَدْنا مُلْكَهُ﴾: "وَشَدَّدْنا" [with doubled dāl] is also permissible, but I do not know anyone who read it so. Its meaning is "We strengthened his kingdom". Part of the strengthening of his kingdom was that his sanctuary (miḥrāb) was guarded every night by thirty-three thousand men.
It has also been said that a man sought his help against another man, claiming that he had taken cattle from him. The defendant denied it, so David asked the claimant for evidence (bayyina), but he could not produce it. Then David saw in his sleep that Allah was commanding him to kill the defendant. David held back and said: it is a dream. Then revelation came to him after that that he should kill him. So he summoned him and informed him that Allah had commanded him to kill him. The defendant said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has not taken me to task for this sin; rather, I killed this man's father treacherously. So David killed him. That was among the things by which Allah exalted him and strengthened his kingdom.
﴿وَآتَيْناهُ الحِكْمَةَ وفَصْلَ الخِطابِ﴾: it has been said about this: that he judges by evidence and oath. It has been said about "فَصْلَ الخِطابِ": that he distinguishes between truth and falsehood. And it has been said: [it is the phrase] "أمّا بَعْدُ" (as for what follows), and he was the first to say "أمّا بَعْدُ".

zajjaj:21-21.t:
﴿وَهَلْ أتاكَ نَبَأُ الخَصْمِ إذْ تَسَوَّرُوا المِحْرابَ﴾: "اَلْمِحْرابُ" is the highest room in the house, and likewise it is the highest place in the mosque; "اَلْمِحْرابُ" here is like an upper chamber (ghurfa). The poet said:
؎رَبَّةُ مِحْرابٍ إذا جِئْتُها ∗∗∗ لَمْ ألْقَها أوْ أرْتَقِي سُلَّما
(Mistress of an upper chamber: when I come to her, I cannot meet her unless I climb a ladder.)
"تَسَوَّرُوا" (they climbed over the wall) indicates height.
He said "اَلْخَصْمِ", whose form is the form of the singular, while "تَسَوَّرُوا" is the form of the plural, because your saying "خَصْمٌ" is suitable for the singular, the dual and the plural, the masculine and the feminine. One says "هَذا خَصْمٌ", "هي خَصْمٌ", "هُما خَصْمٌ" and "هم خَصْمٌ". It is suitable for all of that only because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun): you say "خَصَمْتُهُ، أخْصِمُهُ، خَصْمًا". The meaning is "they two are parties to a dispute (هُما ذَوا خَصْمٍ)" and "they are parties to a dispute (هم ذَوُو خَصْمٍ)". If you say "خُصُومٌ", it is permissible, just as you say "هُما عَدْلٌ" and "هُما ذَوا عَدْلٍ"; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَأشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنكُمْ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 2]. So the meaning of "هُما عَدْلٌ" is "هُما ذَوا عَدْلٍ" (they two are possessors of justice).
Whatever verbal nouns you have used to describe nouns may be kept singular even if you describe a plural with them, and may be kept masculine even if you describe a feminine with them. You say "هو رِضًى" (he is pleasing), "هُما رِضًى", and likewise "هَذِهِ رِضًى".

zajjaj:22-22.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إذْ دَخَلُوا عَلى داوُدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنهُمْ﴾: because they came to him not by the way litigants come, not at their [usual] time, and at a time in which David did not permit anyone to enter upon him; so he found that strange and was alarmed. In fact, two angels were sent to him, who took the form of two men disputing with each other.
﴿قالُوا لا تَخَفْ خَصْمانِ بَغى بَعْضُنا عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾: the reading is with the nominative, and what makes "خَصْمانِ" nominative is "نَحْنُ" (we); the meaning is "we are two litigants (نَحْنُ خَصْمانِ)". Had the speech been "لا تَخَفْ خَصْمَيْنِ بَغى بَعْضُنا عَلى بَعْضٍ", it would be permissible, in the sense of "we have come to you as two litigants (أتَيْناكَ خَصْمَيْنِ)", because he found their coming strange, whereas the coming of litigants was something he was very much used to.
﴿فاحْكم بَيْنَنا بِالحَقِّ ولا تُشْطِطْ﴾, that is: "do not be unjust (لا تَجُرْ)"; one says "أشَطَّ، يُشِطُّ" when one is unjust. It is also read "لا تَشْطُطْ", in the sense of "do not go far from the truth", and likewise "لا تَشْطِطْ", with kasra on the ṭāʾ and fatḥa on the tāʾ, whose meaning is like the meaning of the previous one. The poet said:
؎تَشُطُّ غَدًا دارُ جِيرانِنا ∗∗∗ ولَلدّارُ بَعْدَ غَدٍ أبْعَدُ
(Tomorrow the abode of our neighbours will be far, and the abode the day after tomorrow farther still.)
﴿واهْدِنا إلى سَواءِ الصِّراطِ﴾: to the straight course of the road, that is, "the road of truth".

zajjaj:23-23.t:
﴿تِسْعٌ وتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً﴾: He used the ewe (naʿja) as a metonym (kināya) for a woman. Al-Aʿshā said:
؎فَرَمَيْتُ غُفْلَةَ عَيْنِهِ عَنْ شاتِهِ ∗∗∗ فَأصَبْتُ حَبَّةَ قَلْبِها وطِحالَها
(I shot when his eye was heedless of his ewe, and struck the core of her heart and her spleen.)
By "the ewe (al-shāt)" here he meant the woman.
﴿فَقالَ أكْفِلْنِيها﴾, that is: make me the one who takes charge of her, and you give her up. ﴿وَعَزَّنِي في الخِطابِ﴾: he overcame me in the dispute, that is, he was stronger than me in argument.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
﴿قالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إلى نِعاجِهِ﴾: the meaning is "by his asking for your ewe so that he may add it to his ewes (بِسُؤالِهِ نَعْجَتَكَ لِيَضُمَّها إلى نِعاجِهِ)". ﴿وَإنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الخُلَطاءِ﴾: of the partners; you say "فُلانٌ خَلِيطِي، وشَرِيكِي" (so-and-so is my associate, my partner) with one meaning. ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ وقَلِيلٌ ما هُمْ﴾, that is: "few are they (قَلِيلٌ هُمْ)".
And His saying: ﴿وَظَنَّ داوُدُ أنَّما فَتَنّاهُ﴾, to the end of the verse. It is also read without doubling, "فَتَناهُ", by which the two angels are meant «[Translator's note: i.e. "that the two of them tried him".]». The meaning of "ظَنَّ" is: he was certain, except that it is not the certainty of eyewitnessing; for eyewitnessing, only "عَلِمَ" is said.
﴿فاسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُ وخَرَّ راكِعًا وأنابَ﴾: he remained forty days prostrating, not raising his head, asking Allah's forgiveness for his sin, except for an obligatory prayer and what he could not do without, and his tears did not cease.
It is narrated in the exegesis that the cause of the story of David and the two angels was that Iblīs — may Allah's wrath be upon him — appeared to him in the form of a bird of gold, which landed near him. He went to it to take it, but it moved away; he pursued it, and whenever he was about to reach it, it moved away. While following the bird, David caught sight of a woman bathing, and she caught sight of him, so she covered herself with her hair until it concealed her. It is said that she was the wife of Ūriyā ibn Ḥannān. It is narrated that he wrote to the commander of his army to put Ūriyā in the front in a war that was taking place; so he put him forward and he was killed, and David married her.
It is narrated that ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Whoever says that David, upon him be peace, committed anything suspicious with this woman, I will flog him one hundred and sixty lashes, because whoever falsely accuses someone other than a prophet is flogged eighty lashes, and whoever falsely accuses a prophet is flogged one hundred and sixty lashes."
It was in the exegesis that David wished that Ūriyā would perish so that David could marry his wife. This — and Allah knows best — was only on David's part by way of wishing that it would happen for him without his intending it or working towards the man's death, and Allah counted it as a sin against him because of what he wished. It is also possible that he wrote that this man should be put forward in front of the Ark (al-tābūt) because of his valour and bravery in war, hoping for his sufficiency [in battle], and it happened along with that that he was struck down, and thereby his wife became lawful for him. So he was reproached for loving the wife of a man who had no other, while David had ninety-nine wives; and that was among the sins of the prophets. So when he went to great lengths in repentance and exerted himself in beseeching Allah for pardon, until he almost destroyed himself repenting and clearing himself before Allah of his sin — «[Translator's note: the main clause of this sentence is not completed in the source.]» — and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has described that, saying: ﴿واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ ذا الأيْدِ إنَّهُ أوّابٌ﴾ [Ṣād: 17]. And the saying of ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, "May Allah bless David and have mercy on him", indicates the soundness of this interpretation; and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:26-26.t:
﴿إنّا جَعَلْناكَ خَلِيفَةً في الأرْضِ﴾: on this basis it became permissible to call the caliphs "the vicegerents of Allah on earth (خُلَفاءُ اللَّهِ في الأرْضِ)". ﴿فاحْكم بَيْنَ النّاسِ بِالحَقِّ﴾, that is: by the judgement of Allah, since you are His vicegerent.
And His saying: ﴿بِما نَسُوا يَوْمَ الحِسابِ﴾, that is: by their abandoning work for this Day they became like those who forget, even though they were being warned and reminded.

zajjaj:27-27.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾, to the end of the verse: Allah made known to them that He will punish them for [this] supposition (ẓann); and likewise: ﴿وَظَنُّوا أنَّهم إلَيْنا لا يُرْجَعُونَ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 39]. This was said to them only because they denied the resurrection. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿أفَحَسِبْتُمْ أنَّما خَلَقْناكم عَبَثًا وأنَّكم إلَيْنا لا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 115]: if there were no return, there would be no distinction between the wicked and the righteous. After this: ﴿أمْ نَجْعَلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ كالمُفْسِدِينَ في الأرْضِ﴾ [Ṣād: 28], to the end of the verse. Then He said: ﴿كِتابٌ أنْـزَلْناهُ إلَيْكَ مُبارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آياتِهِ﴾ [Ṣād: 29]; the meaning is: "this is a Book (هَذا كِتابٌ), so that they may reflect on its verses", that is, so that they may think about its verses and about the ends (adbār) of their affairs, that is, their consequences. ﴿وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الألْبابِ﴾ [Ṣād: 29], that is: those possessed of intellects.

zajjaj:30-30.t: ﴿نِعْمَ العَبْدُ إنَّهُ أوّابٌ﴾: the meaning is: "an excellent servant is Solomon (نِعْمَ العَبْدُ سُلَيْمانُ); he is one who turns [to Allah], often returning".

zajjaj:31-31.t:
﴿إذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِالعَشِيِّ الصّافِناتُ الجِيادُ﴾: "اَلصّافِناتُ" are horses standing. The people of the language and the people of exegesis said: "اَلصّافِنُ" is the one standing that bends one of its forelegs or one of its hind legs so that it stands on the tip of its hoof (sunbuk), which is the edge of the hoof; so three of its legs are in contact with the ground, and of one leg only the edge of the hoof touches the ground. The poet said:
؎ألِفَ الصُّفُونَ فَلا يَزالُ كَأنَّهُ ∗∗∗ مِمّا يَقُومُ عَلى الثَّلاثِ كَسِيرا
(He grew used to standing on three legs, so he still seems, from standing on three, as if he were lame.)
Some of them said: "اَلصّافِنُ" is the one standing, whether it bends one of its legs or does not bend it. Horses mostly stand — when they stand — in the ṣāfin posture, because it is as though they alternate between their legs.

zajjaj:32-32.t:
﴿فَقالَ إنِّي أحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الخَيْرِ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّي حَتّى تَوارَتْ بِالحِجابِ﴾: "اَلْخَيْرُ" here means horses (al-khayl). The Prophet ﷺ named Zayd al-Khayl "Zayd al-Khayr". Horses were called "اَلْخَيْرَ" (the good) only because «good is tied to the forelocks of horses», as has come in the ḥadīth.
These horses had come to Solomon from the spoils of an army of his, and he became preoccupied with reviewing them until the sun set and the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr) escaped him.
The people of the language said: "حَتّى تَوارَتْ بِالحِجابِ" means the sun, though the sun has not been mentioned. In this matter I do not reckon that they gave the thinking its due, because in the verse there is an indication pointing to the sun, namely His saying: ﴿إذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِالعَشِيِّ﴾ [Ṣād: 31], and "al-ʿashiyy" has the meaning of "after the sun's decline from the meridian"; [so it is] "until the sun was hidden behind the veil (حَتّى تَوارَتِ الشَّمْسُ بِالحِجابِ)". An implied pronoun (iḍmār) is not permissible unless there has been a mention, or an indication of a mention that stands in place of the mention.
Solomon, because of the awe he inspired, was such that no one dared to approach him to alert him to the time of a prayer. I do not know whether the afternoon prayer was obligatory at that time or not; but his reviewing of the horses occupied him until a time passed in which Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is remembered.
The meaning of "أحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الخَيْرِ" is: I preferred the love of good things (al-khayr) to the remembrance of Allah.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
﴿رُدُّوها عَلَيَّ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحًا بِالسُّوقِ والأعْناقِ﴾: "اَلْمَسْحُ" here, according to what has come in the exegesis, is cutting; it is narrated that he struck their legs and their necks. "سُوقٌ" is the plural of "ساقٌ" (leg), like "دارٌ" and "دُورٌ". Solomon would not have struck their necks unless Allah had permitted that, because He does not make repentance from a sin by means of a great sin.
Some people said: he wiped their necks and legs with water and with his hand. But this — I mean his wiping them with water — does not follow from their having distracted him. Those people only said that because killing them was, in their view, reprehensible; but what Allah permits is not reprehensible. It is possible that that was permitted for Solomon in his time and is forbidden at this time.
Mālik holds that the flesh of horses, mules and donkeys should not be eaten, because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والخَيْلَ والبِغالَ والحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوها وزِينَةً﴾ [al-Naḥl: 8], while He said about camels: ﴿لِتَرْكَبُوا مِنها ومِنها تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 79].

zajjaj:34-34.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنّا سُلَيْمانَ﴾: "فَتَنّا" means "We tested". ﴿وَألْقَيْنا عَلى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that Solomon had a son, and he feared the devils for him, because the devils expected relief from the state they were in through Solomon's death; they said: if a child of his survives, we shall not be freed from what we are in. So he nourished him in the clouds out of concern for him, and he died, and a body was cast upon his throne. It is possible that this was a requital for his sin, and it is possible that it means Allah bereaved him of his child.
Most of what has come in the exegesis is that "جَسَدًا" here is "a devil (شَيْطانٌ)", and that Solomon had been commanded not to marry any woman except from the Children of Israel, but he married from others a woman who worshipped other than Allah. So Allah punished him by stripping him of his kingdom. His kingdom was in his ring, and on entering the bath he handed it to a devil — it has come in the exegesis that he was called "Ṣakhr" — who threw it into the sea. So he remained forty days wandering in the land until he found the ring in the belly of a fish. A devil had taken on his form and sat in his place, and his command was carried out in everything in which Solomon's command had been carried out, except Solomon's wives, until Allah restored his kingdom to him. He said: ﴿فَغَفَرْنا لَهُ ذَلِكَ﴾ [Ṣād: 25], that is, that sin; ﴿وَإنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى وحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾ [Ṣād: 25]: a good place of return. «[Translator's note: the words quoted here, with the reference [Ṣād: 25], occur in the Qur'an at Ṣād 25 about David; the closing words also occur at Ṣād 40 about Solomon. The text is translated as written.]»

zajjaj:35-35.t: ﴿قالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وهَبْ لِي مُلْكًا لا يَنْبَغِي لأحَدٍ مِن بَعْدِي إنَّكَ أنْتَ الوَهّابُ﴾, that is: "grant me a kingdom in which there is a sign indicating my prophethood, such as befits no one after me among human beings who are not prophets, so that it is a sign for him «[Translator's note: i.e. for Solomon.]» indicating that You have forgiven me and restored my prophethood to me". The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿فَسَخَّرْنا لَهُ الرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأمْرِهِ رُخاءً حَيْثُ أصابَ﴾ [Ṣād: 36]. "رُخاءً" means gentle; it has also been said: it blows at his command, not violent, as he likes. ﴿حَيْثُ أصابَ﴾ [Ṣād: 36]: the consensus of the exegetes and the people of the language is that it means wherever he wished; its literal sense is "he aimed (قَصَدَ)". Likewise your saying to the one who answers a question "أصَبْتَ" (you are right), that is, "you aimed [correctly] (قَصَدْتَ)" and did not miss the answer.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
﴿والشَّياطِينَ كُلَّ بَنّاءٍ وغَوّاصٍ﴾: "اَلشَّياطِينَ" is conjoined (nasaq) to "اَلرِّيحَ". His saying "كُلَّ بَنّاءٍ وغَوّاصٍ" indicates that it is of the devils; the meaning is "and We subjected to him every builder among the devils, and every diver (وَسَخَّرْنا لَهُ كُلَّ بِنّاءٍ مِنَ الشَّياطِينِ، وكُلَّ غَوّاصٍ)". Those who built ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ ما يَشاءُ مِن مَحارِيبَ وتَماثِيلَ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 13], and those who dived brought out ornaments for him from the sea.
﴿وَآخَرِينَ مُقَرَّنِينَ في الأصْفادِ﴾ [Ṣād: 38]: the rebellious ones among the jinn, the devils, were subjected to him so that he bound them together in fetters. "اَلْأصْفادُ" are chains of iron. Everything you have bound firmly with iron or anything else, you have "صَفَدْتَهُ"; and everyone to whom you have given a lavish gift, you have "أصْفَدْتَهُ", as though you had given him something by which he is tied [to you] — just as you say to one who acquires wealth as capital to keep: "you have acquired a good holding (قَدِ اتَّخَذْتَ عُقْدَةً جَيِّدَةً)".

zajjaj:39-39.t:
﴿هَذا عَطاؤُنا فامْنُنْ﴾, that is: release whomever you wish of them.
﴿أوْ أمْسِكْ﴾: or detain whomever you wish, and there is no reckoning against you for detaining him. It is possible that "عَطاؤُنا" is what We have given you of wealth, abundance and kingdom; ﴿فامْنُنْ﴾, that is: give from it; ﴿أوْ أمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ﴾: without any favour held over you; or, if you wish, "بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ" means: without requital.

zajjaj:41-41.t:
﴿واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا أيُّوبَ إذْ نادى رَبَّهُ أنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطانُ بِنُصْبٍ وعَذابٍ﴾: "عَبْدَنا" is accusative because the action falls upon it, and "أيُّوبَ" is a badal (substitute) for "عَبْدَنا", because "أيُّوبَ" is the proper name, and a proper name cannot be a naʿt (adjective); it can only be an explanatory badal.
"بِنُصْبٍ", and "نَصَبٍ" with fatḥa on the nūn and the ṣād, and "نُصْبٍ" with ḍamma on the nūn, have one meaning. It has been read "بِنُصْبٍ" with ḍamma on the nūn and sukūn on the ṣād, and it has been read with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the ṣād; and "وَنَصَبٍ", with fatḥa on the nūn and the ṣād, is equivalent to "نُصْبٍ" with ḍamma on the nūn. "اَلنُّصْبُ" and "اَلنَّصَبُ" are like "اَلرُّشْدُ" and "اَلرَّشَدُ", "اَلْبُخْلُ" and "اَلْبَخَلُ", "اَلْعُرْبُ" and "اَلْعَرَبُ". "اَلنَّصْبُ", with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the ṣād, is on the original pattern of the maṣdar (verbal noun); and "اَلنُّصْبُ" and "اَلنَّصَبُ" are in the sense of "نَصَبْتُ، نَصْبًا، ونُصْبًا، ونَصْبًا", on the original pattern of the maṣdar.
The meaning of "بِنُصْبٍ وعَذابٍ" is: with harm in my body and torment in my wealth and my family. It may also be: with harm in my body and torment in it. It is narrated that Job, upon him be peace, remained afflicted for seven years, with worms crawling from his body, and he called upon his Lord: ﴿أنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ وأنْتَ أرْحَمُ الرّاحِمِينَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 83].

zajjaj:42-42.t: ﴿ارْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ﴾: the meaning is "We said to him: strike with your foot (قُلْنا لَهُ: اُرْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ)", meaning "tread the ground with your foot". So he trod the ground lightly once, and a spring gushed forth for him; he washed in it, and the disease left the outside of his body. Then he trod a second time, and water gushed forth and he drank from it, and it washed the disease from the inside of his body.

zajjaj:43-43.t: ﴿وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ أهْلَهُ ومِثْلَهم مَعَهُمْ﴾: it has been said: "وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ أهْلَهُ" means We gave him in the Hereafter the reward for losing them, and gave him in this world the like of them. It has also been said: his family was brought back to life for him, and the like of them was given to him. ﴿رَحْمَةً مِنّا﴾: "رَحْمَةً" is accusative, a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). ﴿وَذِكْرى لأُولِي الألْبابِ﴾: for those possessed of intellects. The meaning of "وَذِكْرى لِأُولِي الألْبابِ" is: when an intelligent person is afflicted, he remembers the affliction of Job and is patient.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
﴿وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثًا﴾: the meaning is "and We said: take in your hand (وَقُلْنا: خُذْ بِيَدِكَ)". "اَلضِّغْثُ" is a bundle of grass, or of sweet basil, or something similar.
It has come in the exegesis that Job's wife said to him: "If only you would seek nearness to the devil and slaughter a young she-goat for him." He said: "Not even a handful of dust." And he swore that, when he was healed, he would flog her a hundred lashes. Allah was grateful to her for her service to him, so He made the expiation of his oath that he should take a bundle containing a hundred twigs and strike her a single blow. People have differed: some said this was particular to Job, upon him be peace, and others said it applies to all people.
﴿أوّابٌ﴾: one who returns often to Allah.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
﴿واذْكُرْ عِبادَنا إبْراهِيمَ وإسْحاقَ ويَعْقُوبَ﴾: whoever says "عِبادَنا" makes "إبْراهِيمَ وإسْحاقَ ويَعْقُوبَ" a badal (substitute) for "عِبادَنا"; and whoever reads "عَبَدْنا" «[Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the singular reading «عَبْدَنا» is meant, as the following sentence shows.]» makes "إبْراهِيمَ" alone the badal, and makes "إسْحاقَ ويَعْقُوبَ" conjoined (ʿaṭf) to His saying "عَبْدَنا".
And His saying: ﴿أُولِي الأيْدِي﴾: it has also been read "اَلْأيْدِ", without yāʾ. The meaning of "أُولِي الأيْدِي" is: possessed of strength in worship. ﴿والأبْصارِ﴾, that is: they are possessed of insight in what brings near to Allah. One may say of a people: "they have hands (أيْدِي) over these", that is, "they have power over them". The poet said:
؎اِعْمَدْ لِما تَعْلُو فَما لَكَ بِالَّذِي ∗∗∗ لا تَسْتَطِيعُ مِنَ الأُمُورِ يَدانِ
(Aim for what you can master, for you have no two hands for matters beyond your power.)
That is: aim for what you can overcome, and do not aim for that in which you will be overcome, that is, for you have no strength [for it]. Whoever reads "أُولِي الأيْدِ", without yāʾ, its meaning is from "اَلتَّأْيِيدُ" (support), and strengthening for something.

zajjaj:46-46.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنّا أخْلَصْناهم بِخالِصَةٍ ذِكْرى الدّارِ﴾: it is also read "بِخالِصَةِ ذِكْرى الدّارِ", with "خالِصَةِ" in genitive construct (iḍāfa) with "ذِكْرى". Whoever reads with tanwīn makes "ذِكْرى الدّارِ" a badal (substitute) for "خالِصَةٍ", and the meaning is "We purified them by the remembrance of the Abode (إنّا أخْلَصْناهم بِذِكْرى الدّارِ)". The meaning of "اَلدّارُ" here is the abode of the Hereafter.
Its interpretation admits two aspects. One of them: "إنّا أخْلَصْناهم" — We made them purely Ours, by making them remind [people] of the abode of the Hereafter and make them renounce this world; and such is the way of the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them. And it may be [that it is] by their frequently remembering the Hereafter and returning to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

zajjaj:47-47.t: ﴿وَإنَّهم عِنْدَنا لَمِنَ المُصْطَفَيْنَ الأخْيارِ﴾, that is: those whom Allah took as His chosen elite; He purified them from all impurities and freed them from them.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
And His saying: ﴿واذْكُرْ إسْماعِيلَ واليَسَعَ وذا الكِفْلِ﴾: it is also read "واللَّيْسَعَ وذا الكِفْلِ". He had taken responsibility (takaffala) for the work of a righteous man; it is said that that man used to pray a hundred prayers every day, and when the righteous man died, Dhū al-Kifl took responsibility for his work and used to do his work. It is also said that Dhū al-Kifl took responsibility for the affair of some prophets and saved them from being killed, so he was named "Dhū al-Kifl".
﴿وَكُلٌّ مِنَ الأخْيارِ﴾: the meaning is "and all of these who have been mentioned are among the best". "اَلْأخْيارُ" is the plural of "خَيِّرٌ", and "أخْيارٌ" is like "مَيِّتٌ" and "أمْواتٌ".

zajjaj:49-49.t:
﴿هَذا ذِكْرٌ وإنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: this is an honour and a fine mention by which they will be remembered forever, and in addition to that they will have a good place of return (maʾāb), that is, a good return: they are mentioned with praise in this world and return in the Hereafter to Allah's forgiveness. Then He explained how good that return is, saying: ﴿جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الأبْوابُ﴾ [Ṣād: 50]. "جَنّاتِ" is a badal (substitute) for "لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ".
The meaning of "مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الأبْوابُ" is: that is, [the gates] of them (مِنها). Some of them said: [it means] "with their gates opened for them (مُفَتَّحَةً لَهم أبْوابُها)", and the meaning is the same; but in terms of Arabic grammatical analysis (taqdīr), "the gates of them (اَلْأبْوابُ مِنها)" is better than making the alif and lām a substitute for the hāʾ and alif, because the meaning of the alif and lām is in no way the meaning of the hāʾ and alif: the hāʾ and alif are a noun (ism), while the alif and lām entered for definiteness, and a particle that came for a meaning is not substituted for a noun, nor does it stand in for it; that is impossible.

zajjaj:52-52.t: ﴿وَعِنْدَهم قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ أتْرابٌ﴾: He means houris who have restrained their glances to their husbands, so they do not look at anyone else. ﴿أتْرابٌ﴾: peers; ﴿وَكَواعِبَ أتْرابًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 33], that is, their ages are one, and they are at the height of youth and beauty.

zajjaj:53-53.t: ﴿هَذا ما تُوعَدُونَ لِيَوْمِ الحِسابِ﴾, that is: for a day on which every soul will be recompensed for what it did. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the bliss of the people of Paradise does not end, saying: ﴿إنَّ هَذا لَرِزْقُنا ما لَهُ مِن نَفادٍ﴾ [Ṣād: 54], that is, it has no ending.

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿هَذا وإنَّ لِلطّاغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ﴾: the meaning is "the matter is this (اَلْأمْرُ هَذا)"; so "هَذا" is nominative, the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). Or, if you wish, "هَذا" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted. And "جَهَنَّمَ" [Ṣād: 56] is a badal (substitute) for "شَرَّ مَآبٍ", that is, an evil place of return.

zajjaj:57-57.t:
﴿هَذا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وغَسّاقٌ﴾: [غَسّاقٌ is read] with the sīn doubled and undoubled. "حَمِيمٌ" is nominative in two respects. One of them is in the sense of "this is scalding water and ghassāq, so let them taste it (هَذا حَمِيمٌ وغَسّاقٌ فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ)". It is also possible that "هَذا" is in the sense of the explanation "this — let them taste it", and then He said afterwards: ﴿حَمِيمٌ وغَسّاقٌ﴾.
It is possible that "هَذا" is in the position of the accusative under this explanation, and possible that it is in the position of the nominative. If it is in the position of the accusative, it is on [the pattern] "let them taste this — let them taste it (فَلْيَذُوقُوا هَذا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ)", as He said: ﴿وَإيّايَ فاتَّقُونِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 41], and like that is "زَيْدًا فاضْرِبْهُ" (Zayd — strike him).
Whoever puts it in the nominative does so as a mubtadaʾ (subject), making the command occupy the position of the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, like ﴿والسّارِقُ والسّارِقَةُ فاقْطَعُوا أيْدِيَهُما﴾ [al-Māʾida: 38].
It has been said that the meaning of "غَسّاقٌ" is the intensely cold, which burns by its coldness. It has also been said that "اَلْغَسّاقُ" is what oozes from the skins of the people of the Fire; if one drop of it were to drip in the East, it would make the people of the West stink, and likewise if it fell in the West.

zajjaj:58-58.t: ﴿وَآخَرُ مِن شَكْلِهِ أزْواجٌ﴾: it is also read "وَأُخَرُ". "آخَرُ" is conjoined to His saying ﴿حَمِيمٌ وغَسّاقٌ﴾ [Ṣād: 57], that is: and another punishment of its kind; He is saying: like that first one. Whoever reads "وَأُخَرُ", the meaning is "and other kinds of its sort (وَأنْواعٌ أُخَرُ مِن شَكْلِهِ)", because His saying ﴿أزْواجٌ﴾ means kinds.

zajjaj:59-59.t: ﴿هَذا فَوْجٌ مُقْتَحِمٌ﴾: "اَلْفَوْجُ" are the followers of the leaders and their companions in misguidance. It was said to them: "لا مَرْحَبًا" (no welcome), [مَرْحَبًا being] accusative, as in your saying "رَحُبَتْ بِلادُكَ مَرْحَبًا" (may your land be spacious) and "صادَفْتَ مَرْحَبًا" (you have met with a welcome); then "لا" was brought in upon that meaning.

zajjaj:60-60.t: ﴿قالُوا بَلْ أنْتُمْ لا مَرْحَبًا بِكم أنْتُمْ قَدَّمْتُمُوهُ لَنا﴾: this is the saying of the followers to the leaders.

zajjaj:61-61.t: ﴿قالُوا رَبَّنا مَن قَدَّمَ لَنا هَذا﴾, to the end of the verse, that is: add to his punishment another punishment. The evidence for this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿رَبَّنا إنّا أطَعْنا سادَتَنا وكُبَراءَنا فَأضَلُّونا السَّبِيلا﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 67] ﴿رَبَّنا آتِهِمْ ضِعْفَيْنِ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 68]; and the meaning of "ضِعْفَيْنِ" is the meaning of "so increase him in punishment, doubled (فَزِدْهُ عَذابًا ضِعْفًا)".

zajjaj:63-63.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أتَّخَذْناهم سِخْرِيًّا﴾: it is read with the alif as a disjunctive hamza (qaṭʿ) with fatḥa, in the sense of a question (istifhām); whoever makes it a conjunctive hamza (waṣl) reads it in the sense of "we indeed took them in mockery (إنّا اتَّخَذْناهم سِخْرِيًّا)". It is read "سِخْرِيًّا" and "سُخْرِيًّا", with kasra and with ḍamma, and the meaning is the same. Some people said: what is from "subjection (al-taskhīr)" has ḍamma on its first letter, and what is from "mockery (al-huzuʾ)" has kasra on its first letter.

zajjaj:64-64.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخاصُمُ أهْلِ النّارِ﴾, that is: the description We have given of them is true. Then He made clear what it is, saying: it is the mutual disputing of the people of the Fire. All of this is in the sense of "when the Day of Resurrection comes, the people of the Fire will say such-and-such"; and likewise everything in the Qur'an that reports [the words] of the people of Paradise and the Fire.

zajjaj:65-65.t: ﴿قُلْ إنَّما أنا مُنْذِرٌ وما مِن إلَهٍ إلا اللَّهُ الواحِدُ القَهّارُ﴾, that is: say that you warn, and that you call to the oneness of Allah. Had it been read "إلّا اللَّهَ الواحِدَ القَهّارَ", in the accusative, it would be permissible; but it has not been read so, so do not ever read it so. Whoever puts it in the accusative does so on the basis of exception (istithnāʾ), and whoever puts it in the nominative does so in the sense of "there is no god but Allah (ما إلَهٌ إلّا اللَّهُ)".

zajjaj:67-67.t: And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُلْ هو نَبَأٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ ﴿أنْتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ [Ṣād: 68], that is: say: the tidings I have given you from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are great tidings, and what I have told you is proof of my prophethood. He means what the Prophet ﷺ told them of the story of Adam and Iblīs, for that can only be known by reading books or by revelation from Allah; and those whom the Prophet ﷺ addressed knew that he had not read any book nor written one with his right hand, and there was no doubt that what he reported was revelation.

zajjaj:69-69.t: Then He made that clear, saying: ﴿ما كانَ لِيَ مِن عِلْمٍ بِالمَلإ الأعْلى إذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾, that is: I did not know these stories except by revelation from Allah.

zajjaj:71-71.t: ﴿إذْ قالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلائِكَةِ إنِّي خالِقٌ بَشَرًا مِن طِينٍ﴾: they are the assembly (al-malaʾ) of the angels; the malaʾ of every town are its prominent people and its best.

zajjaj:75-75.t: ﴿قالَ يا إبْلِيسُ ما مَنَعَكَ أنْ تَسْجُدَ لِما خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ أسْتَكْبَرْتَ﴾: it is read in three ways: "بِيَدَيَّ", as a dual; "بِيَدِيَ أسْتَكْبَرْتَ", with fatḥa on the yāʾ, without doubling, and with "hand" in the singular; and with sukūn on the yāʾ of "hand" and the singular: "بِيَدِي أسْتَكْبَرْتَ".

zajjaj:77-77.t: ﴿قالَ فاخْرُجْ مِنها فَإنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ﴾, that is: for you are accursed; its meaning is: for you are stoned (marjūm) with the curse.

zajjaj:78-78.t: ﴿وَإنَّ عَلَيْكَ لَعْنَتِي إلى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ﴾: the day on which every soul will be requited for what it earned. The meaning of "يَوْمِ الدِّينِ" is: the Day of Recompense.

zajjaj:81-81.t: ﴿إلى يَوْمِ الوَقْتِ المَعْلُومِ﴾: which none knows but Allah; and "يَوْمِ الوَقْتِ" is the Day of Resurrection.

zajjaj:83-83.t: And His saying: ﴿إلا عِبادَكَ مِنهُمُ المُخْلَصِينَ﴾, with fatḥa on the lām: Allah made them pure for His worship. Whoever reads the lām with kasra means only "those who made their religion pure for Allah".

zajjaj:84-84.t: ﴿قالَ فالحَقُّ والحَقَّ أقُولُ﴾: it has also been read "قالَ فالحَقَّ والحَقَّ أقُولُ", with both in the accusative. Whoever puts it in the nominative does so in two ways: in the sense of "for I am the Truth, and the truth I say (فَأنا الحَقُّ والحَقَّ أقُولُ)"; and it may be nominative in the sense of "the truth is from Me (فالحَقُّ مِنِّي)". Whoever puts it in the accusative does so in the sense of "the truth I say; and truly, I will surely fill Hell, truly (فالحَقَّ أقُولُ والحَقَّ لِأمْلَأنَّ جَهَنَّمَ حَقًّا)".

zajjaj:88-88.t: ﴿وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأهُ بَعْدَ حِينٍ﴾, that is: after death.
